concepts.definition: Publisher-stated lifecycle status of the IP right application (application.status), e.g. filed, accepted, granted, lapsed, withdrawn, expired, ceased, unknown. It describes the application's own administrative state at the snapshot; it is not a business status, not evidence of grant or enforceability beyond the stated value, and not a statement about any party. 'ceased' is a publisher-stated application lifecycle state and must not be read as business cessation or as a party's status; 'unknown' is a legitimate publisher-stated state, not a parse failure.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.status is owned by licence and describes an authorisation held by a business; an IP-office application status has a different owner, subject and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date the IP right application was filed/lodged (application.application_date). It is the application's own filing date, not the party-role validity start, not the business establishment date and not a registration date.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.start_date is owned by licence and ext.entity.date_established is owned by business; neither covers the filing date of an IP right application, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated earliest filing date recorded for the IP right application (application.earliest_filed_date), which may precede the current application's own filing date where an earlier filing is carried forward. It is an application-level date, not the party-role validity start and not a business date.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers an earliest-filing date of an IP application; ext.licence.start_date and ext.entity.date_established have different owners and meanings, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated priority date of the IP right application (application.priority_date), the date from which priority is claimed. It is an application-level legal date, not the filing date, not a grant date and not a business date.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept expresses a priority date; ext.licence.start_date and ext.entity.date_established are owned by licence and business respectively, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date on which the IP right application gained registered status (application.gained_registration_status_date). Frequently blank; a blank must not be read as 'never registered'. It is an application-level milestone, not a business incorporation or registration date.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.date_established and ext.entity.prior_registration_state concern business establishment/registration; a registration milestone of an IP application has a different owner and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date on which the IP right application gained enforceable status (application.gained_enforceable_status_date). Frequently blank; a blank must not be read as 'not enforceable'. It is an application-level milestone and does not assert that any right is in fact enforceable against any party.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers an enforceability milestone of an IP application; ext.licence.start_date/end_date are licence validity dates with a different owner and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date from which the IP right application is enforceable (application.enforceable_from_date). The column is entirely empty in this snapshot, so the concept is defined for schema completeness only and no value is asserted; it is not the same as the date enforceable status was gained.
concepts.why_not_existing: No shortlisted concept covers an enforceability start date of an IP application, and ext.licence.start_date is a licence validity start owned by licence, so reuse would change owner and meaning.

concepts.definition: Publisher-stated date on which the IP right application is deemed retired (application.deemed_retired_date). Frequently blank; a blank must not be read as 'still active'. It is an application-level date, not the end of a party-role association and not the end of the business.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.licence.end_date is owned by licence and dyn.party_activity.effective_to_date is owned by party_activity; a deemed-retirement date of an IP application has a different owner and meaning, so reuse would change meaning.

reuse.dyn.ip_application.application_number: Reused: same owner (ip_application), same meaning (IP-office application identifier), same source paths.
reuse.dyn.ip_application.ip_right_type: Reused: same owner and meaning; the application-level classification needed to key the application.
reuse.dyn.ip_application.ip_right_sub_type: Reused: same owner and meaning; application-level sub-classification.
reuse.dyn.party_activity.effective_from_date: Reused: party-role validity start, distinct from the application dates defined here.
reuse.dyn.party_activity.effective_to_date: Reused: party-role validity end, distinct from application.deemed_retired_date.
reuse.dyn.party_activity.is_current: Reused: party-role currency flag, not an application status.
